greek: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ Ιακωβ εἶδεν καὶ ἰδοὺ Ησαυ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ ἐρχόμενος καὶ τετρακόσιοι ἄνδρες μετʼ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐπιδιεῖλεν Ιακωβ τὰ παιδία ἐπὶ Λειαν καὶ Ραχηλ καὶ τὰς δύο παιδίσκας
hint: Seeing Esau coming with four hundred men, Jacob divides the children among Leah, Rachel and the two slave-girls.

notes.text: ἐπιδιαιρέω, *to divide anew*, which Middle Liddell gives that sense and the middle's *to distribute among themselves*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts αὐτός before the second καί, and ἐπί before Ραχηλ.

reading: [[having looked up|having looked up, having looked, having looked up at, having cast up, having recovered one's sight|ἀναβλέπω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] and [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[name:Ησαυ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of him [[coming|coming, going, going back and returning, going to and intending, coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] and four hundred [[men|men, men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of him. and [[divided anew|divided anew, distributed among themselves|ἐπιδιαιρέω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[name:Λειαν]] and [[name:Ραχηλ]] and the two [[young girls|young girls, maidens, young slaves, courtesans|παιδίσκη]]

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")
(Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")
(Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")

greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν τὰς δύο παιδίσκας καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτῶν ἐν πρώτοις καὶ Λειαν καὶ τὰ παιδία αὐτῆς ὀπίσω καὶ Ραχηλ καὶ Ιωσηφ ἐσχάτους.
hint: Jacob ranks them: the slave-girls and their sons first, Leah and hers next, Rachel and Joseph last.

notes.text: ἐν takes the word beside it into the unit; πρῶτος is filed under πρότερος, as at 8:5.

reading: and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] the two [[young girls|young girls, maidens, young slaves, courtesans|παιδίσκη]] and the sons of them [[in first|within, inside of, and by means of first, first and foremost, outermost, first men, first prize, first part and beginning, first and highest, extremities, chief|ἐν; πρῶτος]] and [[name:Λειαν]] and [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] of her [[backwards|backwards, back and back again, again, hereafter, behind, following|ὀπίσω]] and [[name:Ραχηλ]] and [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[outermost|outermost, furthest and uttermost and extreme, last, uppermost, lowest and deepest, innermost|ἔσχατος]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: αὐτὸς δὲ προῆλθεν ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἑπτάκις ἕως τοῦ ἐγγίσαι τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Jacob goes ahead of them and bows to the ground seven times as he nears his brother.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads παρῆλθεν, *went past*.

reading: he [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[went forward|went forward, went on, advanced, went before|προέρχομαι]] [[before|before, in front of|ἔμπροσθεν]] of them and [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped, worshipped, adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated himself before|προσκυνέω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] seven times [[until|until, till, while, so long as|ἕως]] [[of the bringing near|of the bringing near, of the bringing up to, of the approaching, of the being imminent, of the approximating to, of the being next of kin, of the being on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of him.

greek: καὶ προσέδραμεν Ησαυ εἰς συνάντησιν αὐτῷ καὶ περιλαβὼν αὐτὸν ἐφίλησεν καὶ προσέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔκλαυσαν ἀμφότεροι.
hint: Esau runs to meet Jacob, embraces and kisses him, and they both weep.

notes.text: φιλέω, *to love, regard with affection*, where the Hebrew has *kiss*, as through GEN 27 and 29.

reading: and [[ran to|ran to, ran towards and came to, ran up, ran at and made a sally|προστρέχω]] [[name:Ησαυ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] a meeting to him and [[having seized around|having seized around and embraced, having encompassed and surrounded, having intercepted, having got hold of and caught, having comprehended and included|περιλαμβάνω]] him [[loved|loved, regarded with affection, felt affection, loved and cherished, treated affectionately and kindly and welcomed|φιλέω]] and [[fell upon|fell upon, struck against, fell against, attacked and assaulted, ran to, embraced, fell in with and lighted upon and met with|προσπίπτω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the neck|the neck, the throat|τράχηλος]] of him, and [[they wept|they wept, they lamented, they wailed, they wept for|κλαίω]] [[each|each, both of two|ἀμφότερος]].

greek: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἶδεν τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ τὰ παιδία καὶ εἶπεν Τί ταῦτά σοί ἐστιν; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Τὰ παιδία, οἷς ἠλέησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν παῖδά σου.
hint: Esau asks about the women and children: the children, Jacob answers, by which God has shown his servant mercy.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: and [[having looked up|having looked up, having looked, having looked up at, having cast up, having recovered one's sight|ἀναβλέπω]] [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women|γυνή]] and [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] what [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] to you is; the one [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]], to which [[had pity on|had pity on, shewed mercy upon, felt pity|ἐλεέω]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[the child|the child, the son, the daughter, the grandchild, the boy and youth and lad, the girl and maiden, the slave and servant and man and maid|παῖς]] of you.

greek: καὶ προσήγγισαν αἱ παιδίσκαι καὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν,
hint: The slave-girls and their children come near and bow down.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads παιδία, the other word for children.

reading: and [[came near|came near, approached|προσεγγίζω]] [[the young girls|the young girls, the maidens, the young slaves, the courtesans|παιδίσκη]] and [[the things borne|the things borne, the born, the children, the young|τέκνον]] of them and [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped, worshipped, adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated himself before|προσκυνέω]],

greek: καὶ προσήγγισεν Λεια καὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς καὶ προσεκύνησαν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα προσήγγισεν Ραχηλ καὶ Ιωσηφ καὶ προσεκύνησαν.
hint: Leah and her children, then Rachel and Joseph, come near and bow down.

notes.text: προσεγγίζω, one sense, *to approach*; the singular verb with Rachel and Joseph both.

reading: and [[came near|came near, approached|προσεγγίζω]] [[name:Λεια]] and [[the things borne|the things borne, the born, the children, the young|τέκνον]] of her and [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped, worshipped, adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated himself before|προσκυνέω]], and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[came near|came near, approached|προσεγγίζω]] [[name:Ραχηλ]] and [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped, worshipped, adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated himself before|προσκυνέω]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Τί ταῦτά σοί ἐστιν, πᾶσαι αἱ παρεμβολαὶ αὗται, αἷς ἀπήντηκα; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἵνα εὕρῃ ὁ παῖς σου χάριν ἐναντίον σου, κύριε.
hint: Esau asks what all the encampments he met are for; Jacob says they are to find favour with him.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς, *in the eyes of*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] what [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] to you is, [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the insertions|the insertions, the interpolations, the encampments and fortresses|παρεμβολή]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]], to which [[I have moved from|I have moved from and it stands so, I have met, I have met and encountered, I have come|ἀπαντάω]]; the one [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[in order that|in order that, so that|ἵνα]] [[may find|may find, may find out, may discover, may get and gain|εὑρίσκω]] [[the child|the child, the son, the daughter, the grandchild, the boy and youth and lad, the girl and maiden, the slave and servant and man and maid|παῖς]] of you [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight|χάρις]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you, [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ησαυ Ἔστιν μοι πολλά, ἄδελφε· ἔστω σοι τὰ σά.
hint: Esau has plenty, and tells his brother to keep what is his.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] is to me [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long|πολύς]], [[son of the same mother|son of the same mother, brother, near kinsman|ἀδελφός]]; let be to you [[the thy property|the thy property, the thy interests, the thy and thine and of thee|σός]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιακωβ Εἰ εὕρηκα χάριν ἐναντίον σου, δέξαι τὰ δῶρα διὰ τῶν ἐμῶν χειρῶν· ἕνεκεν τούτου εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου, ὡς ἄν τις ἴδοι πρόσωπον θεοῦ, καὶ εὐδοκήσεις με·
hint: Jacob urges Esau to accept the gifts: seeing his face is like seeing the face of God.

notes.text: The potential optative with ἄν: *as one might see*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[if|if, whether, come on|εἰ]] [[I have found|I have found and it stands so, I have found out, I have discovered, I have gotten and gained|εὑρίσκω]] [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight|χάρις]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you, [[take|take, accept, receive, receive in exchange for, take rather and choose|δέχομαι]] [[the gifts|the gifts, the presents, the votive gifts, the blessings|δῶρον]] [[through|through, right through, by means of, by the agency of|διά + genitive]] [[of the mine|of the mine, of the to me and relating to me and against me, of the by me|ἐμός]] [[of hands|of hands, of hands and arms, of arms|χείρ]]; [[on account of|on account of, for the sake of, because of, for, as far as regards|ἕνεκα]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] [[I saw|I saw, I perceived, I beheld, I looked at|ὁράω]] [[the face|the face, the visage, the countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of you, [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] ever [[some|some, any, a certain one|τις]] [[may see|may see, may perceive, may behold, may look at|ὁράω]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, mask, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[of God|of everything that God is by nature, of deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]], and [[you will be well pleased|you will be well pleased, you will consent, you will be glad|εὐδοκέω]] me;

greek: λαβὲ τὰς εὐλογίας μου, ἃς ἤνεγκά σοι, ὅτι ἠλέησέν με ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἔστιν μοι πάντα. καὶ ἐβιάσατο αὐτόν, καὶ ἔλαβεν.
hint: Jacob calls the gifts his blessings and presses them on Esau, who takes them.

notes.text: εὐλογία, *good language* first: the gifts are called blessings, as at 27:12.

reading: [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] [[the good language|the good language, the fine language, the fair speech and specious talk, the eulogy and panegyric, the blessing|εὐλογία]] of me, which [[I bore|I bore, I carried, I bore along, I endured and suffered, I brought and fetched, I brought and offered and presented|φέρω]] to you, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[had pity on|had pity on, shewed mercy upon, felt pity|ἐλεέω]] me [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] and is to me [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]]. and [[overpowered by force|overpowered by force, pressed hard, did violence to, laid violent hands on, forced|βιάζω]] him, and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀπάραντες πορευσόμεθα ἐπʼ εὐθεῖαν.
hint: Esau proposes that they set out and go straight on.

notes.text: The feminine of εὐθύς, of the straight way; the entry the lexicon files for this lemma is the adverb's, *straightway*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads πορευθῶμεν, *let us go*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[having lifted off|having lifted off, having carried off, having taken away, having removed from, having led away, having sailed and marched away and departed, having departed from, having set out on|ἀπαίρω]] [[we will be driven|we will be driven, we will be carried, we will go, we will walk, we will march, we will go across and pass|πορεύομαι]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[straightway|straightway, forthwith, at once, just, directly and simply|εὐθύς]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Ὁ κύριός μου γινώσκει ὅτι τὰ παιδία ἁπαλώτερα καὶ τὰ πρόβατα καὶ αἱ βόες λοχεύονται ἐπʼ ἐμέ· ἐὰν οὖν καταδιώξω αὐτοὺς ἡμέραν μίαν, ἀποθανοῦνται πάντα τὰ κτήνη.
hint: Jacob pleads the tender children and the nursing flocks, which one hard day's driving would kill.

notes.text: λοχεύω, *to bring forth, bear*, in the passive: the flocks are in labour.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to him [[the lord|the lord, the master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] of me [[learns to know|learns to know, perceives, marks, learns, discerns and distinguishes|γινώσκω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] [[softer to the touch|softer to the touch, more tender, fresher, softer and gentler, more soft and delicate|ἁπαλός]] and [[the things that walk forward|the things that walk forward, the cattle, the flocks and herds, the horses, the small cattle, the sheep|πρόβατον]] and [[the bullocks|the bullocks and bulls and oxen, the cows, the oxen, the kine and cattle, the ox-hide shields|βοῦς]] [[are brought forth|are brought forth, are borne, are brought to the birth and attended in childbirth and delivered, are delivered and bear children, are born|λοχεύω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] me; [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] I may pursue closely them [[day|day, day-break, time|ἡμέρα]] [[one|one, a single one, one alone|εἷς]], [[they will die off|they will die off, they will die, they will be put to death, they will be slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the flocks and herds|the flocks and herds, the single beasts, the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]].

greek: προελθέτω ὁ κύριός μου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ παιδός, ἐγὼ δὲ ἐνισχύσω ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ κατὰ σχολὴν τῆς πορεύσεως τῆς ἐναντίον μου καὶ κατὰ πόδα τῶν παιδαρίων ἕως τοῦ με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς τὸν κύριόν μου εἰς Σηιρ.
hint: Jacob asks Esau to go ahead while he follows at the children's pace, until he reaches him in Seir.

notes.text: σχολή, *spare time, leisure*: at the pace the road allows.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ησαυ Καταλείψω μετὰ σοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ μετʼ ἐμοῦ. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἵνα τί τοῦτο; ἱκανὸν ὅτι εὗρον χάριν ἐναντίον σου, κύριε.
hint: Jacob declines Esau's offer of some of his men, content to have found favour.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] [[I will leave behind|I will leave behind, I will leave as an heritage, I will forsake and abandon and leave in the lurch, I will leave remaining, I will leave alone|καταλείπω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the people|of the people, of the men, of the soldiers, of the land-army, of the common men, of the folk, of the Jews, of the Christians|λαός]] of the one [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of me. the one [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[in order that|in order that, so that|ἵνα]] what [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]]; [[becoming|becoming, befitting, sufficing, sufficient and competent, sufficient and adequate and enough, large enough, considerable and long, satisfactory|ἱκανός]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[I found|I found, I found out, I discovered, I got and gained|εὑρίσκω]] [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight|χάρις]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you, [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]].

greek: ἀπέστρεψεν δὲ Ησαυ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ εἰς τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ εἰς Σηιρ.
hint: That day Esau turns back on his way to Seir.

notes.text: ἀποστρέφω in the active, as at 14:16: he turned back.

reading: [[turned|turned, turned back, turned away, turned oneself about, brought back|ἀποστρέφω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] [[in the day|within, inside of, and by means of the day, the day-break, the time|ἐν; ἡμέρα]] [[to that|to that, to the one there, to the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the way|the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method|ὁδός]] of him [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Σηιρ]].

greek: Καὶ Ιακωβ ἀπαίρει εἰς Σκηνάς· καὶ ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ ἐκεῖ οἰκίας καὶ τοῖς κτήνεσιν αὐτοῦ ἐποίησεν σκηνάς· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου Σκηναί.
hint: Jacob moves on to Tents, building houses for himself and tents for his cattle; hence the name Tents.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is Sukkôt, Succoth, the booths; the Greek translates the name, and Rahlfs prints it with a capital.
[[flag]] Rahlfs takes ἑαυτῷ from the Cairo Geniza witness; Codex Alexandrinus reads αὐτῷ.

reading: And [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[lifts off|lifts off, carries off, takes away, removes from, leads away, sails and marches away and departs, departs from, sets out on|ἀπαίρω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Σκηνάς]]; and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] to himself [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[buildings|buildings, houses, dwellings, households and domestic establishments, households and inmates of the house, houses and families from which one is descended|οἰκία]] and [[to the flocks and herds|to the flocks and herds, to the single beasts, to the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] of him [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[covered places|covered places, tents, camps, dwelling-places, temples|σκηνή]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity|τόπος]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] [[name:Σκηναί]].

names.gloss: (Σκηναί, "tents", the Greek of Hebrew Sukkôt, Succoth, the booths)

greek: καὶ ἦλθεν Ιακωβ εἰς Σαλημ πόλιν Σικιμων, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν γῇ Χανααν, ὅτε ἦλθεν ἐκ τῆς Μεσοποταμίας Συρίας, καὶ παρενέβαλεν κατὰ πρόσωπον τῆς πόλεως.
hint: Coming from Mesopotamia of Syria, Jacob reaches Salem, a city of the Shechemites in Canaan, and camps before it.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *šālēm ʿîr šĕkem*, *safe to the city of Shechem*; the Greek reads Salem as a place-name.

reading: and [[came|came, went, went back and returned, were going to and intended, came within a little of and were near|ἔρχομαι]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Σαλημ]] [[city|city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state|πόλις]] of [[name:Σικιμων]], which is [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]], [[when|when, sometimes|ὅτε]] [[came|came, went, went back and returned, were going to and intended, came within a little of and were near|ἔρχομαι]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of the [[name:Μεσοποταμίας]] of [[name:Συρίας]], and [[put in beside|put in beside, inserted, interpolated, interposed, insinuated, put in line with, fell into line and encamped|παρεμβάλλω]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, mask, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[of the city|of the city, of the citadel, of the country, of the body of citizens, of the state|πόλις]].

names.gloss: (Σαλημ, from Hebrew Šālēm, which the Hebrew hears in šālôm, "peace", and which the Hebrew of this verse reads as šālēm, "safe")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)
(Μεσοποταμία, Greek, "the land between the rivers", for Hebrew Paddan-ʾĂrām)
(Συρία, the Greek name of the land; the Hebrew here is Paddan-ʾĂrām)

greek: καὶ ἐκτήσατο τὴν μερίδα τοῦ ἀγροῦ, οὗ ἔστησεν ἐκεῖ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, παρὰ Εμμωρ πατρὸς Συχεμ ἑκατὸν ἀμνῶν
hint: Jacob buys the portion of field where his tent stands from Hamor, father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs.

notes.text: A hundred lambs, where the Hebrew has a hundred *qĕśîṭâ*, a weight of silver the Greek does not name.

reading: and [[procured for himself|procured for himself, got, gained, acquired, brought upon himself and incurred, procured for another|κτάομαι]] [[the part|the part, the portion, the share, the parcel, the contribution, the part and division and class|μερίς]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country|ἀγρός]] , where [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed|ἵστημι]] [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[the covered place|the covered place, the tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple|σκηνή]] of him, [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[of father|of father, of grandfather|πατήρ]] of [[name:Συχεμ]] of a hundred of lambs

names.gloss: (Συχεμ, from Hebrew Šĕkem, "shoulder", the man who bears the city's name)

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο τὸν θεὸν Ισραηλ.
hint: Jacob sets up an altar there and calls on the God of Israel.

notes.text: The middle of ἐπικαλέω, *to call upon*, as at 4:26 and 12:8.

reading: and [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed|ἵστημι]] [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] an altar and [[called upon for himself|called upon for himself, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper or ally, called before him and summoned, challenged|ἐπικαλέω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]].

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
